result.summary: Paging caps plausibly reduce list volume per search but leave overlapping queries and 429 retries untouched, so the outage class can recur. The change also shrinks name and empty-query coverage (750/250 incidents) without proving that is acceptable for large workspaces.

problems.title: Stale searches still run
problems.detail: Nothing aborts or dedupes prior GraphQL searches when the query changes, so each keystroke can still drive up to three list calls to completion while newer searches start.

problems.title: 429 retries multiply load
problems.detail: Each list page can become up to four HTTP attempts on rate limit, which the PR cites as part of the spike but does not change.

problems.title: Shallower name search
problems.detail: Non-reference name search stops after three pages (750 newest incidents), so matches beyond that window are silently omitted.

problems.title: Tests only lock constants
problems.detail: New unit tests assert page counts against mocks; they do not demonstrate rate-limit safety or end-to-end picker behavior under concurrent queries.

result.betterFix: Stop or ignore superseded searches (client abort or server-side coalescing), and disable or sharply limit 429 retries on incident list GETs; then set page/match limits from the 60/min budget and explicitly cap returned candidates if 25 is the product limit.
